questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. Start looking in good time, through official rental sites as well as facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: We were priviledge enough to find housing on our own just 50 meters from the gates to the university park. It was really a gift to live that close - putting the hours together compared to if we had lived 30 minutes away (might be able to find cheaper housing), many hours are saved that could be spent otherwise.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at courses in good time, but also note that there is a 2 week period in the start where you are able to change your course without any problems.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: traveling Quebec (and other parts of Canada)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The great thing about having a course with a small amount of people is that it is easy to become friends with people from Montreal. The locals know best. Montreal has a great food scene, and also some cool clothing stores. Exploring the different boroughs is also very fun: i will highlight Mile end where i think you should at least try Renzo Sandwich and visit Jeans Jeans Jeans.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose one (or two) small courses

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do all the practical stuff in good time. Arrive 1 or 2 weeks before the courses start, where you can "tourist around". If you can afford it, do more than you usually do, e.g. eat more out, travel more, etc. (it is a life time opportunity and your saving taking a hit is not the thing you will regret)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fun things you can do other than museums and stuff: Picnic Electronique, Run in a race (10, half-marathon, or full marathon; it is a good challenge and a great way to do some sight seeing!), Visit the F1 track, Go to bars outside of the center

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: very difficult to say, it was just a really great time

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being away from family and friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
